Investigate two suspected implementation issues in the Ewald lattice sums of treams-rs (Rust core crates/treams-core/src/lattice/). Work ONLY in the git worktree lanes/lat-inv2 (detached at the work-branch head, which includes test-only package R29). Do NOT commit, push, or touch other worktrees (another lane, lanes/docs-r30, is refactoring lattice/ right now — do not edit it). Build/test through scratch: wt.sh (cd lanes/lat-inv2 && scratch: wt.sh help; wt.sh rust-test <filter>). mpmath is available via scratch: wt.sh python or .venv/bin/python; scripts/generate_references.py has mpmath lattice-sum implementations (image sums, spectral/Weyl, Ewald real/reciprocal parts) you can reuse. Delete scratch files under lat-inv2-* at the end; revert any scratch edits and report them.

Both come from sums_tend_to_their_values_on_the_plane_and_axis (crates/treams-core/src/properties/lattice.rs, check_tiny_normal_shift) at explicit Ewald splits:

(b) seed cc a56a5f6516c7c440885997ffc56333acca405c63c21a138d2aa60be08420d1c1. Case: Spherical l=9 m=5, dim 2, rows [[1.3,0,0],[0,1.6900349879218846,0]], bloch/kpar [-1.9366714370780163,-1.4897164178223457,0], r/shift [1.064233523220655,0.16900349879218846,0], k 3.8934456148495555+2.9295482617625925i, eta 1.294840711821749 (3.73 x |automatic split 0.277-0.209i|), normal z, distance 0. The jet/derivatives path returns 'Ewald sum did not converge within the shell limit' while the value-only sum at the same split converges (agrees with the automatic split to 1e-15). The jet converges at eta 1.25.

(c) seed cc 3b5770169cfe78d1c2a70d91524007775be2b32b6bf5d7b1291f290db5b04d90. Case: Spherical l=9 m=1, dim 2, rows diag(1.812186539561217, 1.486578616712043), kpar 0, shift [0.7086231213752138, 0.6217780392741852, 0], k 3.6967030125754947+1.6792835845807719i, explicit real eta 1.2310069444183365, normal z, distance 1e-20. Component 8 (derivative w.r.t. lattice vector a_{0,x}) of the on-plane sum at the explicit split differs by 5.6e-11 (tolerance 3.35e-11) from three paths that agree to 2.5e-15 (off-plane at that split; automatic split on and off the plane). Part moduli 63/66, so no cancellation.

For each:

  1. Reproduce (add the seed to proptest-regressions/properties/lattice.txt in your worktree, or write a scratch #[test] calling the sum directly).
  2. Compare the affected quantities with mpmath (high precision) to establish which path is wrong and by how much.
  3. Find the root cause in lattice/** (e.g. a shell-stopping rule in the jet path that differs from the value path; an on-plane special case for the reciprocal sum's lattice-vector derivative, e.g. a z=0 branch that drops a term or uses a less accurate formula; a convergence criterion that uses the value only, etc.). Point to file:line.
  4. Propose the smallest fix. Then determine whether it would change ANY value that the recorded gate dumps record: run in your worktree, after a scratch implementation of the fix, scratch: wt.sh bitwise, scratch: wt.sh lat, scratch: wt.sh uf, scratch: wt.sh hot (they compare against fixed recordings; 0 differences = no recorded value changed). Report the results. Also run wt.sh rust-test --lib lattice. Then revert the scratch implementation fully (git checkout the source files) but save the fix as a diff to docs-track/lattice-bc-fix.diff, including two pinned cases for recorded_cases_keep_their_properties (look at its RECORDED format) that reproduce (b) and (c) and pass with the fix.
  5. If a fix would change recorded values, still save the diff, and say exactly which records change and by how much.

Report concisely (under 700 words): for (b) and (c): reproduction, mpmath reference and true errors, root cause with file:line, fix, whether recorded values change (gate results), and the diff path.

Lattice Ewald investigation: (b) is a real shell-limit bug, (c) is test tolerance

Of the two, only (b) is a bug in lattice/**. It is fixed by a one-function change. In (c) the on-plane sum is no worse than the off-plane one: both are off mpmath by the same amount, and the property's tolerance is too tight. Both fixes and the two pinned cases are saved together in docs-track/lattice-bc-fix.diff (87 lines; it applies cleanly to the work head).

The worktree's sources are reverted (clean git status). The scratch #[test] and the temporary debug prints are gone, and so are the lat-inv2-* files, including the gate dump folder lat-inv2-gates. Nothing was committed.

(b) seed a56a5f…, l=9 m=5, eta 1.2948

  • Reproduction: called directly, the value-only sum converges, but the jet fails with "Ewald sum did not converge within the shell limit". The failing piece is the reciprocal part's jet.
  • Shell trace: the reciprocal limit is 32 shells. The value path only just makes it: its last two shells are below tolerance exactly at shell 32. The jet's shell 31 adds 1.07e-7 against a tolerance of 4.8e-8, so it runs out of shells.
  • mpmath (direct image sum, 25 digits):
    • S = 245112.59975279460 + 289382.26327390737i
    • dS/dk = −758598.277882664 − 162962.341281917i
    • dS/da0x = −10404112.2666964 − 5068185.20824789i
    • The value-only sum is within 2.6e-16 of S.
    • With the fix, the jet's dS/dk is off by 6e-16 and dS/da0x by 1.1e-15 (relative). It agrees with the automatic split.
  • Root cause: reciprocal_shells, crates/treams-core/src/lattice/shells.rs:232-238, called at ewald.rs:288.
    • It sets the radius to |k| sqrt(1+100|eta|^2), which assumes the reciprocal terms decay like exp(−|q+G|²/(2|k eta|²)).
    • The real decay is exp(−Re(1/(k eta)²)|q+G|²/2). Here k·eta is turned 37° off the real axis, so the decay is only 0.27 of that. At the old radius the terms have fallen to about e^-14, not the assumed e^-50.
    • The value and jet paths use the same stopping rule. The jet just needs more shells, because its derivative terms grow by about |q+G|².
    • The real-space limit (real_shells) already allows for a turned split; the reciprocal one does not.
  • Fix: take the radius as max(old radius, sqrt(100 / Re(1/(k eta)^2))), with the extra term used only when that decay is positive.
    • For real k·eta the new term is 10|k eta|, never above the old radius, so nothing changes there.
    • The maximum only decides when a sum fails. It never moves where a converging sum stops, so values that already succeed stay bit-identical.

(c) seed 3b5770…, l=9 m=1, component 8 (dS/da0x)

  • Reproduction: confirmed. On-plane and off-plane differ by 5.6e-11 against a tolerance of 3.35e-11.
  • Your premise doesn't hold in this worktree. Only the automatic split matches mpmath; both explicit-split paths are off by the same amount.
Path (explicit split unless noted) Error vs mpmath in component 8
mpmath reference: 7.72663294186564276 + 5.84129084444969332i —
On-plane 5.6e-11 (−2.49e-11, +5.03e-11)
Off-plane (1e-20) 5.3e-11 (−5.34e-11, +2.0e-12)
Automatic split, on and off plane 1.4e-15
  • Where the error sits: the real part is accurate (2e-13 against mpmath 27.1372643181427 − 57.3162387043818i). So the error is in the reciprocal part, where both paths are about 5.5e-11 off.
  • Why: the reciprocal part's component-8 terms add up to about 9e3 in modulus for a sum of 66. That is a cancellation by about 130 inside the reciprocal part. 5.5e-11 is about 27 ulps of those term moduli.
  • Not a dropped term: on and off plane use identical shells (19, with the last adding 3.6e-13), and the on-plane exact gamma path is no less accurate than the off-plane series.
  • Root cause: the test, check_tiny_normal_shift in properties/lattice.rs. It allows 64 ulps of |real part| + |reciprocal part| per component, which ignores cancellation within a part.
  • Fix (test only): allow 64 ulps of the largest component modulus of each part instead (about 2e3 here, giving 9e-11 in total). The diff also updates the doc comment and the explanatory comment.

Pinned cases in the diff

Two normal 0 0 1 lines (the (c) one with distance 1e-20) are added to RECORDED after the 1D cylindrical case. recorded_cases_keep_their_properties passes with the fix. Without the shells.rs change, the (b) line fails with NotConverged. I didn't separately run the (c) line against the old tolerance; its numbers reproduce the reported 5.6e-11 exactly.

Gate results with the scratch fix

Check Result
wt.sh bitwise PASS, 0 failing
wt.sh uf OK, 0 differences
wt.sh hot OK, 0 differences
wt.sh rust-test --lib lattice 47 passed
wt.sh lat FAIL, 14 differences

All 14 lat differences are cases that used to fail with the shell limit and now return results. All are at k=12.0, eta13 (the "k12.0/eta13" in the keys) or are rand cases:

  • Error to full jet (11):
    • sw2: r0 5,−5 reciprocal; r1 3,−1 full; r4 6,2 full; r5 7,3 full; r11 5,−5 reciprocal
    • cw2: r0 0,−7 reciprocal; r1 0,6 full; r3 0,−8 full; r4 0,1 reciprocal
    • rand/sw3/15 and rand/sw3/57
  • Jet error code to full jet, value bytes identical (2): sw2/r9 3,2 reciprocal and rand/sw2/68.
  • Error to value-only success, jet still fails (1): sw3/r2 5,0 reciprocal.

No previously recorded successful value changed: every value that recorded "ok" in r4 is byte-identical. Accepting the fix means re-recording these 14 entries. I haven't checked the newly successful values against mpmath; the property tests pass.
